work_related_expenses.title: ATO: Work-related expenses
work_related_expenses.summary: Work-related deductions generally need a direct connection to earning employment income, must not have been reimbursed, and require appropriate records. Private portions are not deductible.
review_questions: Is each expense directly connected to the taxpayer's employment duties?
Was any amount reimbursed by the employer?
Are receipts, calculations and any required diary or logbook records available?
Has any private-use portion been excluded?

rental_expenses.title: ATO: Rental expenses to claim
rental_expenses.summary: Rental costs can have different treatments: some may be immediately deductible, some claimed over several years, and some not deductible. Expenses may need apportionment for private use, partial-year availability, co-ownership or non-commercial rent.
review_questions: Was the property genuinely available for rent for the relevant period?
Do any costs need to be apportioned for private use or co-ownership?
Are capital works and depreciating assets treated over the correct period?
Can the rental interest and other costs be reconciled to supporting records?

business_expenses.title: ATO: Business deductions
business_expenses.summary: A business deduction generally requires a connection to earning assessable business income. Private use must be excluded, and capital or prepaid costs may require a different treatment or timing.
review_questions: How do the expenses relate to the income-producing business activity?
Have private and domestic amounts been excluded?
Do any items require depreciation or another capital treatment?
Are invoices and payment records available?

investment_deductions.title: ATO: Claiming a deduction for interest
investment_deductions.summary: Interest may be deductible where borrowed money is used to acquire income-producing investments. Mixed-purpose borrowing generally requires apportionment, and the use of the borrowed funds is important.
review_questions: Can the use of the borrowed funds be traced to income-producing investments?
Does any private or mixed use require apportionment?
Is corresponding investment income reported?
Are loan statements and interest calculations available?

gifts_and_donations.title: ATO: Gifts and donations
gifts_and_donations.summary: A deductible gift generally must be made to a deductible gift recipient and satisfy the relevant gift conditions. Receipts and evidence of the recipient's status should be retained.
review_questions: Was the recipient endorsed as a deductible gift recipient?
Was the payment a genuine gift rather than a purchase or benefit received?
Is a receipt or other supporting evidence available?

tax_affairs.title: ATO: Cost of managing tax affairs
tax_affairs.summary: Certain costs incurred in managing tax affairs may be deductible. The nature, timing and supporting invoice for each cost should be checked.
review_questions: What service does each fee relate to?
Was the amount incurred by this taxpayer in the relevant period?
Is the invoice or payment record available?

personal_super.title: ATO: Personal super contributions
personal_super.summary: Eligibility to deduct personal super contributions depends on applicable requirements, including giving the fund a valid notice of intent and receiving its acknowledgment before claiming.
review_questions: Was the contribution made to a complying super fund?
Was a valid notice of intent provided within the required timeframe?
Did the fund acknowledge the notice before the deduction was claimed?
Is the claimed amount consistent with contribution records?

general_records.title: ATO: Records you need to keep
general_records.summary: Taxpayers should keep records supporting the income and deductions reported in their return. Records should explain the transaction and allow amounts and calculations to be checked.
review_questions: Can reported amounts be reconciled to source documents?
Are calculation methods and apportionments documented?
Are records complete for unusually large or uncommon items?
